paragraphs: Many companies own lots of vehicles, like buses, vans and hire cars. Since 2023, the law says they must put their vehicle details on a national database.
Gardaí use this database at the roadside. It helps them check if a car has insurance.
But 9,851 company insurance policies still have no vehicle details. Also, almost 25,000 drivers have no driver number on the system.
Insurance Ireland is a group for insurance companies. It wants the Gardaí to be stricter. Companies that break the rule can get a fine of up to €500 for each vehicle.
A road safety group says it is shocked by the numbers. It says Ireland is many years behind the UK.
sentZh: 許多公司擁有大量車輛，例如公車、廂型車和租賃車。
自 2023 年起，法律規定它們必須把車輛資料登錄到一個全國資料庫中。
警察在路邊使用這個資料庫。
它幫助他們檢查一輛車是否有保險。
但有 9,851 份公司保單仍然沒有車輛資料。
此外，系統上將近 25,000 名駕駛人沒有駕照號碼。
Insurance Ireland 是代表保險公司的團體。
它希望警方更加嚴格。
違反規定的公司每輛車最高可被罰款 500 歐元。
一個道路安全團體說，這些數字令他們震驚。
它說愛爾蘭落後英國很多年。

paragraphs: Thousands of company vehicles are missing from a national insurance database, and insurers want the Gardaí to take stronger action.

Since November 2023, the law says that businesses with many vehicles, called fleets, and car sellers must add their vehicles to the National Fleet Database. Gardaí can check this database on their phones at the roadside to see if a vehicle is insured.

However, Minister of State Seán Canney said 9,851 fleet and car trade policies have still not given any vehicle details. Almost 25,000 named drivers are also missing their driver number, which has been required since March 2025.
Moyagh Murdock, head of Insurance Ireland, said the time for a soft approach is over and the rules must now be enforced. Owners who do not follow the law can be fined up to €500 per vehicle.
Susan Gray of the road safety group Parc said she was shocked. She said Ireland is about 15 years behind the UK on this issue.

另有將近 25,000 名列名駕駛人缺少駕照號碼，而這項資料自 2025 年 3 月起即為必填。
Insurance Ireland 負責人 Moyagh Murdock 表示，寬鬆處理的時期已經結束，現在必須執行規定。

道路安全團體 Parc 的 Susan Gray 說她感到震驚。
她說愛爾蘭在這個問題上大約落後英國 15 年。

paragraphs: Insurers have urged gardaí to get tough on businesses that have failed to register the insurance details of almost 10,000 fleet policies on a national database.

Since November 2023, fleet owners and motor traders have been legally required to upload vehicle details to the National Fleet Database, which roadside police units can check on mobile devices. The rules cover buses, delivery vans, hire cars, construction vehicles and many others.

Minister of State Seán Canney revealed in a parliamentary reply that 9,851 fleet or motor trade policies had yet to provide vehicle details. Information from the Motor Insurance Bureau of Ireland also showed that almost 25,000 named drivers lacked driver numbers.

Insurance Ireland chief executive Moyagh Murdock said the initial soft approach had ended and compliance was now a matter of enforcement. Offenders face fines of up to €500 per vehicle, and she warned that law-abiding drivers are effectively subsidising those who break the rules.
Susan Gray of the road safety group Parc said she was shocked by the figures, adding that Ireland lags around 15 years behind the UK.
